Read the status records of receiver logs

Source: R/read_receiver_logs.R
read_receiver_logs.Rd

Reads the records a receiver writes about itself, as opposed to its detections: hourly temperature, noise, tilt and pulse counts, battery and memory, and events such as a reboot, a pause in recording, a fault, the initialisation and the download. audit_listening() reads them, through its logs argument, as evidence that a receiver was running on a day it heard nothing.

Usage

read_receiver_logs(file, format = "vdat")

Arguments

file

Path to a VDAT CSV file, or several paths. Several files are read one by one and stacked, with their name in source_file.

format

"vdat", the one format read so far; VUE receiver-event CSV files are not read yet.

Value

A data frame, one row per record: receiver_serial (the bare serial, as deployment sheets write it), receiver_model, datetime (UTC), record_type (the VDAT record type), temperature_c, noise, noise_unit ("mV" or "dB"), tilt_deg, depth_m, pings and log_detections (pulses and detections counted since the receiver's previous DIAG record), battery_v, battery_pct, memory_pct, event (an event's type or a fault's importance), event_detail (an event's subtype, description and values, which is where a NexTrak writes its text, or a fault's description and code) and source_file. A field the record does not carry is NA. The attribute source holds one record per file: the file, the format version, the rows kept, the DIAG records, the DATA_ERROR

records and the records found by type.

Details

Format. "vdat" reads a Fathom VDAT CSV (VEMCO DATA LOG), the CSV that Fathom Connect or VDAT writes from a receiver's VRL or VDAT file; the same file read_detections() reads for detections. The VRL or VDAT file itself is binary, and a zip archive holds other files: each stops with a message that says to export it with Fathom Connect, or to unzip it. Formats 1.0.0 and 2.0.0 are read. The records kept are DIAG and DIAG_NEXTRAK (ambient temperature, noise, tilt, depth, and the pulses and detections counted since the last record), TEMP, ATTITUDE, BATTERY, HEALTH_VR2TX and HEALTH_NEXTRAK, which are the status records, and EVENT, EVENT_FAULT, EVENT_INIT and EVENT_OFFLOAD. Detections and configuration records are skipped. A VR2Tx writes its status records hourly; a NexTrak writes DIAG_NEXTRAK every 10 minutes and gives noise in dB where a VR2Tx gives mV. A file with no status record, as the exports of a VR2Tx-RLD file are, gives no rows, and a message counts such files.

Receivers and exports read. Checked against field exports, with the records read matching the records each file holds: VR2Tx-69 receivers, format 2.0.0, as exported by VDAT 13.9.0, 14.10.1 and 15.1.1; and NexTrak-R1 receivers, format 2.0.0, as exported by VDAT 13.2.2, 13.9.0 and 15.1.1 and by Fathom Connect 4.0 and 4.1. Format 1.0.0 is read from its layout and is not tested on a field export. Other models and versions may read; they have not been checked. The yearly receiver-event CSV files that VUE exports are not read.

What a file may lack. A NexTrak export of Fathom Connect 4.0 can lack the DIAG_NEXTRAK record, and with it the noise, pings and detection counts. A file with status records and no DIAG or DIAG_NEXTRAK record is named in a message; its noise, pings and log_detections are NA, and audit_listening() reads its other status records. DATA_ERROR records carry no time or serial, so they are not rows of the table; a message counts them, and attr(, "source") gives the count per file.

Time. datetime is the receiver's corrected Time at the row's Time Offset (h), as read_detections() reads it, or the uncorrected Device Time (UTC) where Time is blank. Both are written in UTC.

Damaged files. A file of 0 bytes stops with its name. A last line cut part-way, with no line end, is dropped with a warning, and a file that declares an EVENT_OFFLOAD record but holds none is named in a warning, as in read_detections(). A file that is not a VDAT CSV, such as a VUE detection export, stops with its name and what to use instead.

See also

audit_listening(), read_detections()

Examples

# The synthetic logs of the example study, one file per receiver
log_files <- list.files(system.file("extdata", "receiver_logs", package = "detqc"),
                        full.names = TRUE)
logs <- read_receiver_logs(log_files)
table(logs$record_type)
#> 
#>          DIAG         EVENT    EVENT_INIT EVENT_OFFLOAD  HEALTH_VR2TX 
#>          4537             1            19            19           187 
#>          TEMP 
#>          4537 
head(logs[logs$record_type == "DIAG", c("receiver_serial", "datetime", "noise",
                                        "noise_unit", "pings")], 3)
#>   receiver_serial            datetime noise noise_unit pings
#> 2            R001 2024-06-01 14:00:00   301         mV   360
#> 4            R001 2024-06-01 15:00:00   302         mV   360
#> 6            R001 2024-06-01 16:00:00   303         mV   360
# A synthetic NexTrak log: DIAG_NEXTRAK every 10 minutes, noise in dB
nextrak <- read_receiver_logs(system.file("extdata", "nextrak_receiver_log.csv",
                                          package = "detqc"))
table(nextrak$record_type)
#> 
#>   DIAG_NEXTRAK          EVENT     EVENT_INIT  EVENT_OFFLOAD HEALTH_NEXTRAK 
#>            288              1              1              1            288
